# PLAN020 plan-variant-as-arm

An input-chosen alternative is modeled as an outcome arm.

## What it does

A scenario that `realizes` a goal variant is checked against the other variants of the same goal. An outcome arm of that scenario whose label is the name of such a sibling variant is flagged at the arm: the alternative is chosen twice, once as a goal variant and once as an outcome.

## Why it matters

A choice made by the input (a role, an intent) is a goal variant; a choice made by the outcome of a step is an arm. Writing the same alternative both ways splits one decision across two places that can drift apart.

## Remedy

Realize the sibling variant from its own scenario and keep only genuine step outcomes as arms.

## Examples

### Fires case 1

```grmb expect=fire file=design/model.grmb
grimble = "2";
module m;

system s {
  ambient escalate { verified_by "tests/a.py"; }
  actor u : human;
  step u.pick : { ok, cash };

  goal u { start; }
  goal u.start { one_of { card; cash; } }

  scenario t realizes u.start.card {
    u.pick => {
      ok => end ok;
      cash => end err(cash);
    }
  }
}
```

### Clean case 2

```grmb expect=clean file=design/model.grmb
grimble = "2";
module m;

system s {
  ambient escalate { verified_by "tests/a.py"; }
  actor u : human;
  step u.pick : { ok, declined };

  goal u { start; }
  goal u.start { one_of { card; cash; } }

  scenario t realizes u.start.card {
    u.pick => {
      ok => end ok;
      declined => end err(declined);
    }
  }
}
```
